subject: Literature
title: Simone de Beauvoir's The Second Sex
description: A short lesson to help you apply Simone de Beauvoir's The Second Sex.

hook.text: Simone de Beauvoir wrote 'One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman' — one sentence that transformed feminist thought.

buildup.text: The Second Sex, published in 1949, examined how society constructs femininity and confines women to the role of 'Other.'

discovery.text: Beauvoir argued that gender is not biology but a social construction, anticipating decades of feminist and gender theory.

twist.text: The Vatican placed the book on its Index of Forbidden Books, and critics called it immoral and dangerous.

climax.text: The Second Sex became the intellectual foundation of second-wave feminism and remains essential reading worldwide.

punchline.text: One sentence rewrote how the world understood gender.

quiz.question: What was Beauvoir's revolutionary argument about gender?
options: Women are biologically superior to men
Gender is not biology but a social construction
Men and women should live in entirely separate societies
